ORIGINAL CONTRIBUTIONS: ESOPHAGUS

# Effect of Running on Gastroesophageal Reflux and Reflux Mechanisms

*   Thomas V K Herregods
*   Froukje B van Hoeij
*   Jacobus M Oors
*   Albert J Bredenoord
*   André J P M Smout

Authors and Affiliations

American Journal of Gastroenterology111(7):p 940-946, July 2016. | DOI: 10.1038/ajg.2016.122

Abstract

## OBJECTIVES:

**Reflux symptoms are common among athletes and can have a negative impact on athletic performance. The aim of this study was to investigate the effect of exercise on reflux severity and examine the underlying reflux mechanisms.**

## METHODS:

**Healthy sporty volunteers were studied using both high-resolution manometry and pH-impedance monitoring. After a meal and a rest period, subjects ran on a treadmill for 30 min at 60% of maximum heart rate, followed by a short rest period and another 20-min period of running at 85% of maximum heart rate.**

## RESULTS:

**Ten healthy volunteers were included. Exercise led to a significantly higher percentage of time with an esophageal pH<4 and a higher frequency and duration of reflux episodes.**
